## Exploring Data Types in ArcGIS Online

This lesson will focus more on the different types of data available in
ArcGIS Online, and how to import your own data.

Annotation vs geospatial data - using feature data layers rather than
sketches (Did we really do sketches in part 1?)

- Raster versus vector data
- Living Atlas data
- Import & export

Raster/DEM - Lat/Long CSV file - uploading your own dataset and/or
finding a dataset in living atlas

Features have attributes - a data table/tabular data - columns have
fixed data types (a lot of them) - for example bikes

Raster/DEM - Lat/Long CSV file - uploading your own dataset and/or
finding a dataset in living atlas

Types of data:

- Vector: Difference between point, line, and polygon
- Raster: an array of values that can be used
  - Single band
  - Multibands

How to add a new data layer: - Import point data from a csv, lat/long
csv file - Raster/DEM - Importing or uploading a dataset vs finding a
good dataset in living atlas

- Facilities data (buildings)
- DEM (expanded to the foothills)
- Bike paths (a newly extended to roads version)
- Bus stops (lat-long csv file. for when you get tired)

Esri ArcGIS Online Credits:

- All ArcGIS Online accounts created under the UCSB site license are
  allocated **1000 service credits** per license year.

- Transactions: Some analysis operations use credits. For more
  information, visit Esri's [Understand
  Credits](https://doc.arcgis.com/en/arcgis-online/administer/credits.htm)
  Page.

- Manage your content: Periodically review and delete unnecessary
  content.

- Data Stewardship: Objects stored in ArcGIS Online should be considered
  ephemeral. The content depends on your access to the UCSB Library's
  Higher Education Site License.

### Digital Elevation Models

Add DEM (a 1 channel raster) - `ucsb_local_dem` - Explain data - Show
where it came from - Explore stats

Applying color schemes \* 'Stretch' on gray is the default. Change it to
a below and above zero diverging scheme \*

![](images/Workshop2/dem_options.png)

Can make a hillshade on the fly from here \* Duplicate layer. Rename the
2 dem layers. Make the bottom one a shaded relief \* Choose morning or
night and summer or winter with the shaded relief controls

Explain azimuth and altitude. Our output will have the scene lit from
the west, with the sun pretty low in winter.

![](images/Workshop2/relief_options.png)

- Highlight steepest route (max slope)
